land.text: 'In 771, King Offa of Mercia conquered the territory of the Haestingas', and 'By 772 he apparently controlled the whole of the Kingdom of Sussex'

successors.note: Cliopatria ends its Sussex row in 771 and grows its Mercia shape in 772. The Sussex infobox: 'Subject to Mercia: 771 to c. 796', 'Subject to Wessex again: from c. 827', 'Full integration into the crown of Wessex: 860'; the Ellendun page calls it 'hitherto under direct Mercian rule' in 825. The years 796-827 are not settled by the pages opened. [Reviewer eu-11-b: the infobox status line reads 'Independent kingdom (477–686, 715–771, 796–827) Client state of Wessex (686–715, 827–860) Client state of Mercia (771–796)'; the dossier follows the text ('By 772 he apparently controlled the whole of the Kingdom of Sussex') and the Ellendun page ('hitherto under direct Mercian rule'), so the Mercia and Wessex dossiers decide 772-860.]

capitals.name: Chichester
capitals.note: The page says 'it is unlikely that they would have had a capital in Sussex'. Chichester, said by legend to take its name from Cissa, is shown as the conventional centre only; the first see was Wilfrid's monastery at Selsey and the bishopric moved to Chichester in 1075.

correction.text: the later county of Sussex, to which the kingdom's 'boundaries coincided in general'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Sussex row begins in 490, but the page gives the foundation as 477 ('in 477 Ælle and his three sons arrived in three ships') and notes that 'many academics place this about 20 years earlier, c. 457'. The corrected outline is the later county of Sussex, not the Cliopatria shape, which reaches into Hampshire (see the 490 verdict).

correction.text: the later county of Sussex; the Meonwara are added by the 661 gain

keyframe_review.note: 490-691, 5,657 km2. Gazetteer check (the infobox gives no area): the Cliopatria outline resolves to 5,817 km2 against 4,046 km2 for the region Sussex, a ratio of 1.44, within the factor of two; the extra 9 cells lie in south-east Hampshire. The page puts the Meonwara (Meon valley) in Sussex only by Wulfhere's gift, so until the 661 gain the outline should be the county; the ledger adds the Meon valley in 661 (Wulfhere page) and keeps it to 771. From 686 Sussex was 'subject to Wessex' (c. 686 to c. 715) although Cliopatria draws it as free to 691.

correction.text: Sussex as in 718, 692-717: a vassal of Wessex from c. 686 to c. 715 with its own kings

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Sussex shape for 692-717, yet the kingdom had its own kings under West Saxon rule: 'In 692 a grant is made by a king called Noðhelm (or Nunna)', 'In 710 Sussex was still under West Saxon domination', and Nunna's last charter is 'dated 714 in error for 717'. The 718 outline is carried back. The page is silent on whether Sussex kept the Meon valley after Cædwalla.

718-762, 5,657 km2. Sussex had broken away 'some time before 722'; the Chronicle records a further West Saxon campaign in 725 with no recorded outcome. Kings Æðelstan, Æðelberht and Ealdwulf (a grant 'until about 765') appear. Gazetteer check (the infobox gives no area): the Cliopatria outline resolves to 5,817 km2 against 4,046 km2 for the region Sussex, a ratio of 1.44, within the factor of two; the extra 9 cells lie in south-east Hampshire.

763-767, 5,701 km2 (0.8 percent above the 718 shape, Cliopatria noise). 'In 765 and 770 grants are made by a King Osmund'; Offa confirmed the 770 grant. Gazetteer check (the infobox gives no area): the Cliopatria outline resolves to 5,817 km2 against 4,046 km2 for the region Sussex, a ratio of 1.44, within the factor of two; the extra 9 cells lie in south-east Hampshire.

768-771, 5,701 km2. Last shape before Offa's conquest of the Haestingas in 771. Gazetteer check (the infobox gives no area): the Cliopatria outline resolves to 5,817 km2 against 4,046 km2 for the region Sussex, a ratio of 1.44, within the factor of two; the extra 9 cells lie in south-east Hampshire.

correction.text: Sussex in 772 without the Haestingas, whom Offa conquered in 771; the rest passes to Mercia that year

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Sussex shape for 772, but the page has 'By 772 he apparently controlled the whole of the Kingdom of Sussex', so 772 is the last year; the Haestingas are already Offa's from 771 and the remainder passes to Mercia in 772.

region.text: the South Saxons' kingdom, whose 'boundaries coincided in general with those of the later county of Sussex'

ledger.note: 477: Ælle and his three sons land and found the South Saxon kingdom. 'In 477 Ælle and his three sons arrived in three ships'; infobox 'Established: c. 477', though 'many academics place this about 20 years earlier, c. 457'. The tradition is the Chronicle's, not a contemporary record.

region.text: Andredadsceaster, identified with Anderitum, modern Pevensey

ledger.note: 491: Ælle takes the Saxon Shore fort of Andredadsceaster (Pevensey). 'his siege of the Saxon Shore fort at Andredadsceaster' took place 'in 491,' after which 'the inhabitants were massacred'. The page names the fort, not a frontier; the outline already includes it in Cliopatria's 490 shape.

region.text: the Meonwara, the Meon valley and the Hampshire coast beyond the later county of Sussex (Cliopatria's western extension)

ledger.note: 661: Wulfhere of Mercia gives Æthelwealh the Meonwara. 'Wulfhere raided the Isle of Wight in 661. He then gave the island and the Meonware (the Meon valley) to his godson, King Æthelwealh of the South Saxons.' The Sussex page says only that Wulfhere gave him 'the Isle of Wight and the Meonwara (Meon valley)' at his baptism, with no year; the year follows the Wulfhere page's sequence.

661: the Isle of Wight is given to Sussex. 'Wulfhere of Mercia conquered the island in 661 and gave overlordship to his godson, King Æthelwealh of Sussex', to convert the islanders. The page says Sussex, not South Saxons. Suzerain's record: the counterpart is the island's kingdom.

686: Cædwalla of Wessex conquers the Isle of Wight. Bede records that 'the island was converted after an invasion in 686 by King Cædwalla of Wessex'; 'After this point, the island became a part of Wessex and later England.'

region.text: the South Saxons' kingdom, whose 'boundaries coincided in general with those of the later county of Sussex'

ledger.note: c. 686: Sussex falls under West Saxon rule. Infobox 'Subject to Wessex: c. 686 to c. 715'; Cædwalla killed Æthelwealh (c. 685, Cædwalla page), was expelled by the ealdormen Berhthun and Andhun, and 'Once on the throne, Cædwalla attacked the South Saxons again, this time killing Berthun'. The vassal's record: the counterpart is the overlord.

region.text: the South Saxons' kingdom, whose 'boundaries coincided in general with those of the later county of Sussex'

ledger.note: c. 715: Sussex shakes off Wessex. Infobox 'Subject to Wessex: c. 686 to c. 715'; 'In 710 Sussex was still under West Saxon domination' and Sussex broke away 'some time before 722'.

region.text: the territory of the Haestingas, the people of Hastings

ledger.note: 771: Offa of Mercia conquers the Haestingas. 'In 771, King Offa of Mercia conquered the territory of the Haestingas'; the Offa page has Symeon of Durham saying Offa defeated 'the people of Hastings' and doubts the charters, putting his direct involvement at about 770-771.

region.text: the rest of the kingdom of the South Saxons

ledger.note: 772: Offa holds all of Sussex. 'By 772 he apparently controlled the whole of the Kingdom of Sussex'; infobox 'Subject to Mercia: 771 to c. 796'. The Offa page says western Sussex kings recognised him early and the east less readily, with no Mercian trace between 772 and c. 790.

wars.name: West Saxon-South Saxon fighting of 607
wars.outcome: The page records only 'when Ceolwulf of Wessex fought against the South Saxons'; no land is said to change hands.

wars.name: Cædwalla's conquest of Sussex

zones.text: the South Saxons' kingdom, whose 'boundaries coincided in general with those of the later county of Sussex'

wars.outcome: Cædwalla killed Æthelwealh c. 685, was driven out by the ealdormen Berhthun and Andhun, and on becoming king of Wessex 'attacked the South Saxons again, this time killing Berthun'; Sussex was subject to Wessex c. 686 to c. 715.
wars.note: The Cædwalla page gives no year for the second attack; the Chronicle's 685 is 'began to contend for the kingdom'.

wars.name: West Saxon campaign against Sussex (725)
wars.outcome: The Chronicle 'records a further West Saxon campaign in 725'; the page gives no outcome and Sussex is not recorded as subject again.
wars.note: The Ine of Wessex page was not opened within the budget.

wars.name: Offa's conquest of Sussex

zones.text: the territory of the Haestingas, the people of Hastings
the South Saxons' kingdom, whose 'boundaries coincided in general with those of the later county of Sussex'

wars.outcome: Offa conquered the Haestingas in 771 and 'By 772 he apparently controlled the whole of the Kingdom of Sussex'; Sussex was 'subject to Mercia' from 771 to c. 796.
wars.note: The Offa page doubts the charters that show his control of Sussex and limits his direct involvement to about 770-771.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on any page opened: the frontier with Kent, Surrey and Hampshire is the later county line taken as approximate; the Meon valley edge is the least certain.

notes: Cliopatria's Sussex outline reaches Southampton Water (bbox west to -1.47), 9 cells beyond the county; this dossier keeps the county until the Meonwara gift (bridged to 661) and then Cliopatria's western extension, flagged at confidence 2 (year from the Wulfhere page, region Cliopatria's). Cliopatria ends Sussex in 771; the dossier ends it in 772 on the page's 'By 772'. Mirror events needed from other dossiers: Wessex (vassal_start c. 686 and vassal_end c. 715 with counterpart kingdom-of-sussex; the 686 gain of the Isle of Wight), Mercia (gain of the Haestingas 771 and of the rest 772). The Sussex page sets 796-827 apart (Mercian subjection to c. 796, Wessex again from c. 827), the Ellendun page has direct Mercian rule to 825 and conquest by Wessex in 825; both are after this dossier's end and belong to Mercia's and Wessex's dossiers. Not dated by the pages opened: Ælle's bretwalda overlordship south of the Humber; Cissa. Ine's campaigns of 722/725 rest on the Sussex page alone (Ine of Wessex page not opened). Gazetteer names needed: Chichester and Pevensey are not in places.jsonl (used only as a coordinate and a radius). The page gives no infobox area.
